**Opening argument: the answer is 32.**

The conjugacy quandle $\mathcal{Q}(G)$ records exactly the conjugation action of $G$ on itself. An isomorphism $\mathcal{Q}(G_1)\cong\mathcal{Q}(G_2)$ therefore forces the groups to share the same structure of inner automorphisms and commutator relations. Isoclinism is the equivalence relation that captures precisely this kind of shared commutator data, so for small orders the two notions line up. That is the pattern the solution documents: for every order below 32, any two groups with isomorphic conjugacy quandles are isoclinic.

The solution then locates the first failure at order 32. Groups of order 32 are numerous enough to contain non-isoclinic pairs whose commutator maps and central quotients are compatible with a single quandle isomorphism. The solution cites the classification of small groups and their isoclinism families as the basis for this, and that classification is what makes the claim checkable.

Debater B must therefore show one of two things. Either a pair of non-isoclinic groups of some order below 32 has isomorphic conjugacy quandles, which would contradict the exhaustive check, or the order-32 pair fails to be non-isoclinic or fails to have isomorphic quandles. Without such a counterexample, the minimum is 32.

The answer is $\boxed{32}$.
